title: A Cipher for the Witness
premise: Kestrel Coldharbour, archivist of Saint Verity's Cathedral and keeper of its sealed crypt, is drawn into a murder investigation when the victim is found wearing clothes stolen from Kestrel's own closet — a message meant for him alone. As he digs into the cathedral's inheritance records, he realizes the killer is following a decades-old case file that only three people ever read: Kestrel's late mentor, the bishop who sealed the crypt, and Kestrel himself. The murders reenact an unsolved disappearance from 1974, and each new body brings the killer closer to forcing Kestrel to confess what he found in the crypt as a boy. In the end, Kestrel traps the killer — his mentor's daughter, avenging her father's erased legacy — by offering her the truth instead of a trial, choosing loyalty to the dead over the institution that corrupted them all.
about_author: August Ashgrove is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing ecclesiastical archives before turning to crime fiction. They write mysteries about institutions, secrets, and the people paid to keep both.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Kestrel Coldharbour catalogs the cathedral archive and locks the crypt as he has every night for twenty years. POV: Kestrel. Establishes his pride in closed cases and his ritualized control. Emotional beat: quiet unease when he notices the crypt seal has been disturbed — wax melted from the inside.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Police summon Kestrel: a man found dead in the cloister garth, dressed in Kestrel's own stolen tweed coat and scarf. POV: Kestrel, with Detective Inspector Sorrel Vance observing him. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into resolve — this was staged for him, and he refuses to be a prop.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Losses
chapters.summary: Kestrel audits his own belongings and finds the theft predates the murder by weeks; someone lived inside his routines. POV: Kestrel. He begins a private case file, mirroring the killer's presumed method. Emotional beat: paranoia replacing professional confidence.

chapters.title: What Bishop Anselm Sealed
chapters.summary: Kestrel pulls the 1974 file on the disappearance of archivist Tobias Merrow — the case that led to the crypt being locked. POV: Kestrel, with flashbacks to his apprenticeship under Merrow's successor. Emotional beat: dread, as he recognizes the murder scene mirrors the file's first exhibit.

chapters.title: Detective Vance's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vance interviews Kestrel formally; his knowledge of the old case makes him suspect number one. POV: alternating Kestrel and Vance. Emotional beat: adversarial friction with an undertone of mutual recognition — both are people who trust records over people.

chapters.title: The Second Reenactment
chapters.summary: A second body appears in the chapter house, arranged exactly like exhibit four of the 1974 file — a detail never made public. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: cold fear; the killer isn't guessing, they've read the original file, which means an insider or its author.

chapters.title: Three Readers
chapters.summary: Kestrel narrows the file's readership to three: himself, the late mentor Father Ivo, and Bishop Anselm. POV: Kestrel. He exhumes Ivo's papers and finds pages razored out. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into determination.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Visited
chapters.summary: Kestrel learns Ivo had a daughter, Wren, who visited the archive yearly until she stopped twelve years ago. POV: Kestrel interviewing cathedral staff. Emotional beat: first glimmer of the human cost behind the institutional record.

chapters.title: Anselm's Bargain
chapters.summary: The dying bishop summons Kestrel and offers him a deanship in exchange for letting the past stay buried. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: temptation — power offered precisely because he's compromised, revealing how corruption recruits.

chapters.title: Exhibit Nine
chapters.summary: A third murder recreates exhibit nine: the file's photograph of a child — young Kestrel, taken the day he first entered the crypt. POV: Vance discovering the scene, Kestrel arriving after. Emotional beat: violation; the killer knows Kestrel's childhood secret.

chapters.title: What I Saw at Eleven
chapters.summary: Kestrel confesses to Vance, partially: as a boy he saw Merrow alive inside the crypt, days after the official disappearance. POV: Kestrel, in the longest flashback of the book. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud, and relief that doesn't last.

chapters.title: The File That Lies
chapters.summary: Comparing the 1974 file against physical evidence, Kestrel proves it was doctored — by his own mentor, Ivo, to protect the bishop. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: betrayal; the man whose memory he built his integrity upon was the first corruptor.

chapters.title: Wren Ivo's Testimony
chapters.summary: Vance locates Wren living under another name; she agrees to talk but vanishes before the interview. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into alarm — they may have driven her into the killer's orbit, or she is the killer.

chapters.title: The Fourth Exhibit, Prepared
chapters.summary: Kestrel receives a package: photographs of himself, annotated like evidence exhibits, ending with tomorrow's date. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: hunter becoming quarry; the final reenactment will star him.

chapters.title: Vance Closes In
chapters.summary: Vance traces the stolen clothes to a dry cleaner near Wren's address and moves to arrest her. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: triumph undercut by doubt — the evidence is too neat, curated, almost archival.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Reading Room
chapters.summary: Kestrel realizes the frame is deliberate: the killer wants him to solve it wrong. He feeds Vance false confirmation while preparing his own trap in the archive reading room. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: cold clarity; he will use the killer's love of the file against her.

chapters.title: Night in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Kestrel stages a fake exhibit ten — the confession page missing from Ivo's file — and waits. Wren comes for it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: taut suspense breaking into confrontation between two people orphaned by the same lie.

chapters.title: The Killer's Case File
chapters.summary: Wren reveals her father documented everything before his death and she has spent her life completing his unfinished case. She forces Kestrel toward the crypt at knifepoint. POV: Wren, then Kestrel. Emotional beat: righteous fury meeting complicit guilt.

chapters.title: Inside the Crypt
chapters.summary: In the sealed crypt, Wren demands Kestrel open Merrow's hidden ledger proving the bishop's crimes. Kestrel opens the crypt fully for the first time in fifty years. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: awe and terror as the institution's rot is literally unsealed.

chapters.title: Loyalty or Truth
chapters.summary: Confronted with proof, Kestrel must choose: destroy the ledger to protect the cathedral and Wren goes free, or publish it and condemn them both. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the thematic crux — he chooses truth, but on his terms.

chapters.title: The Confession Page
chapters.summary: Kestrel hands Vance the complete, restored case file — including Ivo's forged pages and the bishop's crimes — and lets Wren surrender rather than die for a cause the record can now carry. POV: Vance. Emotional beat: sorrowful justice; the archive outlives everyone's loyalties.

chapters.title: Recatalogued
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Kestrel reopens the crypt as a public archive, resigns his ambitions of deanship, and files his own account of the case — closing it honestly for the first time. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; some cases close only when the truth does.
